name: Remote API Client
description: Async abstraction over commercial AI APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google). Implements a RemoteClient protocol/ABC with concrete implementations per provider. Handles: auth via env vars, httpx async requests, retry with exponential backoff (configurable max retries), error recovery (rate limits, transient failures, auth errors). Tracks per-request cost using provider-specific pricing tables (input/output token counts × price). Supports a primary provider for live serving/ground-truth and optional additional providers for training data diversity (same input sent to additional providers, responses stored but not used as ground truth). Reports cost per request back to caller for budget accounting. Returns structured TaskResponse or raises typed errors. Uses dual Protocol + ABC pattern: RemoteClient protocol for consumer type hints and lightweight test mocks, BaseRemoteClient ABC for shared retry/cost-tracking/logging logic, and concrete implementations (AnthropicClient, OpenAIClient, GoogleClient) extending the ABC with provider-specific request/response translation via httpx.

types.name: PricingTable

fields.name: entries
fields.description: Dict mapping model name (str) to TokenPricing. Keys are model identifiers as used by the provider API (e.g. 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514', 'gpt-4o'). Values are TokenPricing instances.

types.name: RetryConfig

fields.name: max_retries
fields.description: Maximum number of retry attempts before raising an error. Does not count the initial attempt.

fields.name: base_delay_seconds
fields.description: Base delay in seconds for the first retry. Subsequent retries double this value (with jitter).

fields.name: max_delay_seconds
fields.description: Maximum delay cap in seconds for any single retry wait.

fields.name: respect_retry_after
fields.description: If true, when a Retry-After header is present in a 429 response, use that value instead of calculated backoff (capped at max_delay_seconds).

types.description: Configuration for exponential backoff retry behavior. Full-jitter strategy: delay = random(0, min(max_delay_seconds, base_delay_seconds * 2^attempt)).

types.name: TimeoutConfig

fields.name: connect_timeout_seconds
fields.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for a TCP connection to be established.

fields.name: read_timeout_seconds
fields.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for data to be received after connection is established.

fields.name: total_timeout_seconds
fields.description: Maximum total time in seconds for the entire request (connect + send + read).

types.description: Timeout settings for httpx async requests to the provider API.

types.name: RemoteClientConfig

fields.name: provider

fields.name: model

fields.name: api_key_env_var
fields.description: Name of the environment variable containing the API key (e.g. 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'). The key is read at construction time and stored as SecretStr. Fails fast if the env var is missing or empty.

validators.error_message: api_key_env_var must be a non-empty string

fields.name: retry
fields.description: Retry/backoff configuration for this client.

fields.name: timeout
fields.description: Timeout settings for HTTP requests.

fields.name: pricing_overrides
fields.description: Optional pricing overrides. If provided, these take precedence over built-in default pricing tables for cost calculation. Allows config-driven pricing updates without code changes.

types.description: Configuration for a single remote API client instance. One config per provider. API key is stored as Pydantic SecretStr sourced from environment variables. Validated strictly at construction time — missing or empty API keys cause immediate failure.

types.name: TaskResponse

fields.name: content
fields.description: The text content of the model's response/completion.

fields.name: model
fields.description: The model identifier that actually generated this response (may differ from requested model if provider aliases).

fields.name: provider

fields.name: usage
fields.description: Token usage breakdown for this request/response.

fields.name: cost_usd
fields.description: Computed cost in USD for this request: (input_tokens × input_cost_per_token) + (output_tokens × output_cost_per_token).

fields.name: latency_ms
fields.description: Wall-clock latency in milliseconds from request send to response received (excludes retry wait time, measures only the successful attempt).

fields.name: request_id

types.description: Frozen Pydantic model representing a successful structured response from a remote AI provider. Returned to callers for both live serving and training data collection.

types.name: DiversityResult

fields.name: primary
fields.description: The response from the primary provider, used as ground-truth for serving and evaluation.

fields.name: secondary
fields.description: List of SecondaryResult — one per secondary provider. Each is either a TaskResponse on success or ErrorInfo on failure. Order corresponds to the order of secondary clients provided.

fields.description: Sum of cost_usd across primary and all successful secondary responses. Does not include cost for failed secondary requests (they incurred no billable completion).

types.description: Result of a multi-provider diversity request. Contains the primary provider's response (which is the ground-truth) and secondary responses (which may be successes or captured errors). Secondary failures do not cause the overall operation to fail.

functions.name: create_remote_client
functions.description: Factory function that constructs a concrete RemoteClient implementation for the specified provider. Reads the API key from the environment variable specified in config, validates it is present and non-empty, constructs an httpx.AsyncClient with the configured timeout settings, and returns the provider-specific client instance. Fails fast on missing API key or invalid config. The returned client satisfies the RemoteClient protocol.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Configuration specifying provider, model, auth, retry, timeout, and pricing settings.

inputs.name: http_client
inputs.description: Optional pre-configured httpx.AsyncClient instance for dependency injection. If None, a new client is created internally and the RemoteClient takes ownership (will close it on cleanup). Type is httpx.AsyncClient | None.

functions.name: send_request
functions.description: Send a prompt to the configured remote AI provider and return a structured TaskResponse. This is the primary interface method on the RemoteClient protocol. Internally dispatches through the ABC's _request_with_retry template method, which handles exponential backoff with full jitter. The concrete implementation translates the prompt into provider-specific API format, sends via httpx, parses the response, extracts token usage, computes cost from the pricing table, and measures latency. Generates a UUID4 request_id for audit correlation. Logs each attempt and final result as structured JSON.

inputs.name: messages
inputs.description: Ordered list of PromptMessage forming the conversation prompt. Must contain at least one message with role 'user'.

inputs.name: params
inputs.description: Generation parameters controlling model output behavior.

functions.name: send_diversity_request
functions.description: Send the same prompt to a primary provider and zero or more secondary providers concurrently for training data diversity. The primary provider's response is the ground-truth used for serving. Secondary providers' responses are collected for training data diversity but are not used as ground truth. Uses asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True) to fan out requests concurrently. If the primary provider fails, the entire operation fails with the primary's error. Secondary failures are captured as ErrorInfo in the result without failing the overall operation. Total cost is the sum of all successful responses' costs.

functions.name: compute_cost
functions.description: Pure function that computes the USD cost of a single API request given token usage and pricing. Used internally by clients and available publicly for cost estimation/forecasting without making actual API calls.
postconditions: Return value == (usage.input_tokens * pricing.input_cost_per_token) + (usage.output_tokens * pricing.output_cost_per_token)

functions.name: get_pricing
functions.description: Look up the TokenPricing for a given provider and model. Checks config-provided pricing overrides first, then falls back to built-in default pricing tables. Returns None if no pricing is found for the model (caller must handle missing pricing — typically log a warning and use zero-cost fallback).

inputs.description: The model identifier to look up pricing for.

inputs.name: pricing_overrides
inputs.description: Config-provided pricing overrides that take precedence over defaults.

postconditions: If model exists in pricing_overrides, return that TokenPricing
Else if model exists in built-in defaults for provider, return that TokenPricing
Else return None

functions.name: close
functions.description: Async cleanup method on RemoteClient. Closes the underlying httpx.AsyncClient if this client owns it (i.e., it was not injected externally). If the httpx client was injected, this is a no-op — the caller retains ownership and responsibility for closing it. Safe to call multiple times.
postconditions: If client owns the httpx.AsyncClient, it is closed after this call
If client does not own the httpx.AsyncClient, no action is taken
Subsequent calls to send_request on a closed owned client will raise RuntimeError
Multiple calls to close are safe (idempotent)

structured_side_effects.description: Logs client closure at DEBUG level

invariants: All public functions and methods are fully type-annotated and return Pydantic models or primitive types
API keys are never logged, serialized, or exposed — stored only as Pydantic SecretStr
Auth validation happens at construction time — missing or empty API keys cause immediate AuthError, never deferred to first request
Retry logic uses full-jitter exponential backoff: delay = random(0, min(max_delay, base_delay * 2^attempt))
Auth errors (401/403) and invalid request errors (400/422) are never retried — only 429 and 5xx/connection/timeout errors are retried
If respect_retry_after is true and a 429 response includes a Retry-After header, that value is used instead of calculated backoff (capped at max_delay_seconds)
cost_usd on every TaskResponse is always computed as (input_tokens × input_cost_per_token) + (output_tokens × output_cost_per_token)
Every request generates a unique UUID4 request_id for audit trail correlation across logs
httpx.AsyncClient ownership is tracked: clients created internally are closed by close(), injected clients are left to their owner
All error types carry provider, message, request_id, retries_attempted, and status_code for structured logging and audit
DiversityResult.total_cost_usd == primary.cost_usd + sum of successful secondary cost_usd values
Secondary provider failures in diversity requests are captured as ErrorInfo, never raised as exceptions
Primary provider failure in diversity requests propagates as the corresponding typed error
No global state — all state (config, http client, pricing) flows through constructor parameters or method arguments
Structured JSON logging at all levels using Python stdlib logging with a JSON formatter
Each source file stays under 300 lines — module is split across protocol, ABC, concrete implementations, types, errors, pool, pricing, and factory
